metaDescription: Six compact 4-1/2 inch circular saws compared on motor power, depth of cut, weight, guides and corded versus cordless, for DIY, crafts and tight cuts.
expertTake: The WORX WX439L is the compact circular saw to buy if you want a well known corded design that cuts stock up to 2 inches thick with one hand. The WORKPRO X Series is the cordless pick, with a brushless motor and a 4.0 Ah battery. If you cut full sheets of plywood or dimensional framing lumber, skip compact saws entirely, since their shallow depth and small motors are built for trim, crafts and light stock. Buy on cut depth first and extras second.
introParagraphs: A compact circular saw uses a 4-1/2 inch blade or smaller and a lighter motor, so it is easy to hold in one hand and easy to store in a drawer. That makes it ideal for flooring, trim, crafts and small cuts, but it also limits depth and power in ways the box does not make obvious.
This guide explains how blade size, depth of cut and motor power change what a compact saw can do, and where corded and cordless versions differ.

products.name: WORX WX439L 4.5 Amp 4-1/2 Inch Compact Circular Saw

specList.label: Depth adjust
specList.value: Lever with raise and lower handle

products.description:
The WORX WX439L has a slim body, a 4.5 amp motor and a 4,000 rpm blade, and it is designed for one hand cuts. It handles stock up to 2 inches thick, which covers 2x lumber at a shallow angle. A lever lets you raise or lower the main handle to set depth.

Compared with the Dekopro 5A and Dovaman 5.8A it has a smaller motor but a more established design. Against a full size circular saw it is much lighter, and it is meant for quick cuts around the house. It is a good choice for flooring, trim and small projects.

Blades are small, so keep spares and use a fine tooth blade for plywood. Clean dust from the guard and the base. Its slim shape also fits tight drawers and tool bags, which is a quiet advantage for a saw you use occasionally.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who want a compact saw for trim and small lumber.
pros: Slim body makes one hand cuts easy
Cuts stock up to 2 inches thick
cons: Blade size limits depth of cut

products.name: WORKPRO X Series 20V 4-1/2 Inch Brushless Mini Circular Saw
products.description:
The WORKPRO X Series is a cordless mini saw with a brushless motor at 4,000 rpm and a 4.0 Ah battery. It cuts up to 43 mm deep at 90 degrees and bevels from 0 to 45 degrees. Brushless efficiency stretches the battery across more cuts.

Compared with the older WORKPRO 20V model at 4,500 rpm, it drops some speed but adds the brushless motor. Against the corded WORX it frees you from the cord, with less sustained power. It suits trim, flooring and craft cuts away from outlets.

The battery is proprietary, so check the platform before buying other tools. Store the pack at partial charge. Bring a second battery on longer jobs, since compact saws drain fast on 3/4 inch stock.
products.bestFor: Cordless trim and flooring work with a brushless motor.

products.name: WORKPRO 20V 4-1/2 Inch Cordless Mini Circular Saw with Laser
products.description:
The WORKPRO 20V mini saw runs at 4,500 rpm, higher than the X Series, with a laser guide and three blades in the kit. A 4.0 Ah battery comes with it. An ergonomic rubberized handle supports one hand use.

Compared with the X Series it is a brushed design, which uses more battery per cut. The included blades make it a good starter kit. It suits crafts, trim and plastic sheets.

Test the laser against a test cut before relying on it. Keep the guard clean. The included blades are best kept for rough cuts so the good blade stays sharp.
products.bestFor: Beginners who want a cordless starter kit with extra blades.
pros: 4,500 rpm for fast cuts in thin stock
Rubberized handle for one hand use

products.name: Dovaman 5.8 Amp 4-1/2 Inch Compact Circular Saw with Laser

specList.label: Blades supplied
specList.value: 6 for wood, soft metal and tile

products.description:
The Dovaman has a 5.8 amp motor, the strongest of the corded compact saws here, plus a laser guide, an edge guide and a metal auxiliary handle that mounts on either side. It ships with six blades for wood, soft metal and other materials. That flexibility is its selling point.

Compared with the WORX WX439L it offers more motor power and more accessories, though the WORX has a refined slim body. Against the Dekopro 5A it has a stronger motor. It suits multi material crafts and renovation.

Blades vary in quality, so use them for light jobs. Keep the edge guide tight and the cord clear. Metal blades in the kit make it useful for thin soft metal sheet, but wear eye protection.
products.bestFor: Multi material projects needing blades and guides.
pros: 5.8 amp is the strongest compact motor
Laser and edge guide aid accuracy
Auxiliary handle fits left or right

products.name: Dekopro 5A 4,500 rpm Compact Electric Circular Saw
products.description:
The Dekopro compact saw uses a 600 W, 5 amp motor at 4,500 rpm and weighs 2.1 kg, about 4.6 lb. A parallel guideway helps with straight cuts, and a dual safety switch prevents accidental starts. Three 85 mm blades are included.

Compared with the Extbtfor it has slightly more power and the same light weight. Against the WORX it offers a parallel guide. It suits crafts and thin stock.

The blades are small and soft, so cut within limits. Clean dust from the vents. Light weight also means you should clamp the stock firmly before every cut.
products.bestFor: Craft and model work where light weight matters.

products.name: Extbtfor 4.8A 4-1/2 Inch Corded Mini Circular Saw with Laser
products.description:
The Extbtfor mini saw has a 580 W, 4.8 amp motor at 4,000 rpm, a laser guide and a maximum cutting depth of 1-11/16 inches. It weighs 4.7 lb and can be lifted with one hand. The bevel reaches 45 degrees.

Compared with the WORX WX439L it cuts a little shallower, and it costs less. Against the Dovaman it has a smaller motor. For small cuts in plywood and trim it works well.

Expect a lighter build and basic accessories. Use fresh blades and keep the cord clear. Check that the laser stays aligned after transport, since small knocks shift it.
products.bestFor: Occasional small cuts on a tight budget.
pros: Low cost with a laser guide
4.7 lb is easy to lift with one hand

buyingCriteria.criterion: Blade size and depth of cut
buyingCriteria.explanation: Compact saws use 4-1/2 inch or smaller blades and cut shallower than 7-1/4 inch saws. The Extbtfor lists 1-11/16 inches and the WORKPRO X Series up to 43 mm, about 1-11/16 inches. The WORX WX439L handles stock up to 2 inches. Check depth against the thickest board you cut. A common buyer mistake is to read the 90 degree depth and forget the bevel: at 45 degrees the usable depth falls by roughly 30 percent, so a 1-11/16 inch saw may only cut about 1-1/4 inches at an angle. Test on scrap if you plan to bevel thick boards.

Amp ratings run from 4.5 on the WORX to 5.8 on the Dovaman. More amps help in dense stock, while 4.5 amps is fine for plywood and trim. A weak motor stalls and burns the blade. Do not buy a compact saw for hardwoods. Pushing a small motor through hardwood makes the blade bind, overheats the windings and produces burn marks. Slow the feed and let the blade do the work, and pick a saw with more amps if you cut oak or maple.

Corded saws like the WORX and Dovaman give steady power. Cordless saws like the WORKPRO X Series free you from outlets, with a battery that limits sustained cuts. A brushless motor extends run time. Choose based on where you cut. Cordless saws also lose speed as the battery drains, so cuts at the end of a charge can burn. A spare battery is the cheapest upgrade, and a brushless motor like the WORKPRO X Series stretches each charge.

The Dekopro weighs 2.1 kg and the Extbtfor 4.7 lb, light enough for one hand. Lighter saws are easier to guide and tire you less. Avoid one hand cuts that put your other hand near the blade. A one hand grip is convenient but not always safe, so clamp the work and keep the free hand behind the blade path. Lightweight saws also kick back more readily, so use both hands on long cuts.

Lasers help, but they must be aligned. A parallel guide or edge guide, as on the Dekopro and Dovaman, keeps cuts straight. Use a clamped straightedge for the best accuracy. For trim and flooring, clamp a straightedge to the work and run the shoe along it for perfect lines. The built in guides are a backup, not a replacement for a good straight edge.

Blades for wood, soft metal and tile differ. The Dovaman includes six blades, while the WORKPRO 20V includes three. Use the right blade for the material. Do not cut metal with a wood blade. Small blades are cheap, so buy a few extra and swap as soon as the cut slows. Match tooth count to the material: more teeth for plywood and laminate, fewer for rough lumber.

specDecoder.meaning: The current the motor draws, from 4.5 amps on the WORX to 5.8 amps on the Dovaman. It shows the motor class.
specDecoder.watchFor: Watts and amps appear together in listings, so match units. Always compare the same units across brands.

specDecoder.meaning: Blade speed with no cut, such as 4,000 on the WORX and 4,500 on the Dekopro. It drops under load.
specDecoder.watchFor: Higher rpm does not mean more cutting power. Always compare the same units across brands.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum cut depth with the shoe flat, such as 1-11/16 inches on the Extbtfor.
specDecoder.watchFor: Depth shrinks at 45 degrees. Always compare the same units across brands.

specDecoder.meaning: A motor without brushes, as on the WORKPRO X Series. It runs cooler and extends battery life.
specDecoder.watchFor: Brushed models are cheaper but use more power.

specDecoder.meaning: A line projected onto the work to show the cut path. It helps alignment.
specDecoder.watchFor: It may be off, so test it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cutting capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared blade size and depth, with the WORX at 2 inches and the Extbtfor at 1-11/16 inches. Bevel depth was also considered.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor and power
howWeEvaluated.description: We ranked amp ratings, from 4.5 on the WORX to 5.8 on the Dovaman, and credited brushless motors. Brushed and brushless motors were weighed for run time.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at weight and one hand design, with the Dekopro at 2.1 kg. Balance matters as much as weight for one hand use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Accuracy aids
howWeEvaluated.description: Lasers, edge guides and parallel guides were considered. Accuracy aids came last, since a good straightedge beats a laser.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The WORX leads overall, the WORKPRO X Series for cordless and the Dovaman for accessories. The Extbtfor is the budget pick. Accessory counts were weighed lightly against build quality.

cards.label: Corded
cards.text: Steady power with no battery. The WORX, Dovaman, Dekopro and Extbtfor fit here.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: Freedom from outlets with a battery. The WORKPRO X Series and WORKPRO 20V fit here.

howToChoose.note: Choose corded for bench work and cordless for flooring and remote cuts.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A light saw, an accurate guide and a fine tooth blade. Flooring needs clean edges. Cordless helps with outlets.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The WORKPRO X Series suits cordless work. The WORX WX439L is best for corded cuts.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You cut often and want one hand control. The WORX or WORKPRO X Series repays the cost.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You make occasional small cuts. The Extbtfor or Dekopro is enough.

maintenance.why: Small blades dull quickly. A fresh blade protects the motor.
Dust sticks guards. A clean guard returns smoothly.
A damaged cord is a hazard.
Partial charge extends life for cordless models.

faq.q: What can a compact circular saw cut?
faq.a: Plywood, trim, flooring and 2x lumber at shallow depth. It is not for framing. For anything over 2 inches or long structural cuts, a 7-1/4 inch saw is the right tool.
Cordless is more convenient, while corded is steadier. Compact saws suit both. Corded saws are usually the better value, since the battery and charger add significant cost.
Only with the right blade, such as soft metal blades supplied with some kits. Never cut stainless or hard steel with these saws.
About 1-11/16 to 2 inches at 90 degrees. Less at a bevel. Measure your board and subtract extra for any bevel before trusting the depth number.
It is a convenience. A clamped straightedge gives better accuracy. A cheap laser can shift out of alignment, so treat it as a rough indicator only.

faq.q: Is it safe for one hand use?
faq.a: It is designed for it, but keep the other hand clear and clamp the work. Wear eye protection, since compact saws throw chips toward the user.
